    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.
    • Investors and traders mentioned that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the tech giant and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.
    • It has been revealed that "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you blink, you may have missed it.

    Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

    Investors and traders mentioned that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the tech giant and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

    It has been revealed that "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," stated Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back.".

    "All the same issues that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

    The day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

    Mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also said there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

    According to recent reports, jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he mentioned, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

    The national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

    Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

    Industry observers note that "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) mentioned in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.".

    House Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the company does so much international business.

    "This is an export control matter," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue.".

    Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong problem for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

    In a recent development, "You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," mentioned Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here.".

    To be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

    Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

    But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

    Industry observers note that "Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On his 26th birthday and in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game, Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum starred with 184 rushing yards during a 26-13 win over the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.
    • Corum became the first Rams player to carry the ball at least 30 times in a game during the Sean McVay era.
    • Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love threw a pair of interceptions and could have had a couple more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On his 26th birthday and in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game, Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum starred with 184 rushing yards during a 26-13 win over the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

    Corum became the first Rams player to carry the ball at least 30 times in a game during the Sean McVay era. Meanwhile, the Packers' offense floundered after losing wide receiver Christian Watson to a concussion late in the first half.

    Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love threw a pair of interceptions and could have had a couple more. His team mustered a mere 55 total yards of offense in the second half.

    Industry observers note that mcVay, previously 0-5 against Packers head coach Matt LaFleur, finally beat his former assistant. The Rams (7-4) have won five straight games. Green Bay (6-5) remains last in a crowded NFC North.

    Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons, playing in his first game in nearly a year after tearing an ACL and meniscus in his left knee against the Denver Broncos in Week 15 last season, recorded a long-awaited sack.

    Watson left the game twice: first with a thigh injury after making a 6-yard catch on the opening play from scrimmage and then for the concussion caused by a massive hit near the sideline late in the second quarter for which Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected.

    Forging forward without wide receivers Puka Nacua — who is reportedly out for the season after undergoing MCL surgery — and Davante Adams — who was still sidelined by a hamstring injury — the Rams managed to stake themselves to a 13-3 advantage, scoring on their first three possessions.

    Stafford, who finished with 140 yards on 16-of-23 passing, made do with his lesser-known receivers. A 37-yard defensive pass interference penalty catapulted L.A.'s first drive. That ended with a 43-yard Brandon McManus field goal. McManus trotted back out to kick a 41-yarder following a Rams takeaway later in the opening frame. L.A. linebacker Nate Landman, forcing his eighth regular-season fumble in the past two seasons, punched the ball free from the grasp of Packers tight end Tucker Kraft.

    A 32-yard connection between Love and Watson put the wheels in motion for Green Bay. Rookie kicker Trey Smack, who came in with just 15 makes on 21 field-goal attempts, got the Packers on the board with a 54-yard kick.

    That's when Stafford answered with the kind of efficiency that made him the league MVP last season. He went 5 of 6, at one point keeping the series alive with a clutch dump-off to running back Kyren Williams despite duress on third-and-5. It wasn't long before Williams was surging through the middle for a 7-yard touchdown run to make it a two-score game.

    A pair of highlight-reel plays thrust Green Bay right back into the thick of things. LaFleur turned to trickery initially, with wideout Savion Williams taking a handoff and throwing the ball back to Love, who went on to fling a pass downfield to Watson. His toe-tapping 21-yard reception was followed by a 39-yard catch and run from another receiver, Matthew Golden.

    Sources indicate that watson was the one who found pay dirt, reeling in a 6-yard touchdown pass from Love midway through the second quarter. That score cut the Packers' deficit to 13-10.

    Watson's night came to a premature end on Green Bay's next drive. LaFleur rolled the dice on fourth-and-1 from the L.A. 30-yard line, and it originally looked like that decision was going to be rewarded. Love located Watson for what would have been a chains-moving pickup, except the pass was broken up by a brutal blow from Kinchens near the sideline that leveled Watson.

    Kinchens was ejected because, per the Netflix broadcast, he left his feet and made forcible contact to the head/neck area with his helmet.

    Offsetting penalties — Golden was flagged for offensive pass interference — brought up another fourth-and-1. That time, Smack was sent out for a 48-yard field-goal attempt.

    In a recent development, with that boot, it was 13-13. It remained that way heading into the break.

    According to recent reports, wednesday was a game of attrition. Not only did the Packers lose Watson, but the Rams watched a pair of tight ends — Davis Allen (ankle) and Tyler Higbee (chest) — go out, along with left guard Bill Murray (ankle).

    Even so, L.A.'s offense kept churning. It relied heavily on Corum. The ascending third-year pro from Michigan carried the rock nine times on a 14-play, eight-plus-minute drive that began the third quarter. Corum scored from a yard out to restore the Rams' lead.

    While dominating possession, the Rams eventually established a cushion — that was after Stafford and Love traded interceptions. The latter took place in L.A. territory, as miscommunication between Love and Golden cost the Packers dearly.

    A 35-yard Corum run set the stage for the third of McManus' four field goals.

    Sources indicate that although Love converted a fourth-and-8 with a strike to wideout Bo Melton down the stretch, he tossed his second pick the next snap. Rams cornerback Emmanuel Forbes Jr. dropped deep into coverage and climbed the ladder to force the Packers' third turnover.

    In a recent development, L.A.'s roster may be depleted, but McVay's group is overcoming that cascade of injuries with toughness. The Rams have now rushed for at least 200 yards in back-to-back games.

    Sources indicate that "Our identity going into this game was the most physical team's gonna win," Corum said during his on-field postgame interview. "And I think we showed that today. It's something to build on.".

    Blake Corum is easily the player of the game for LA. The RB finishes with 184 yards and a TD on 32 rushes.

    The Rams improve to 7-4 and remain in the thick of the playoff picture.

    Packers fall to 6-5 and have some ground to make up in the wild-card race.

    In a recent development, LA hits a chip-shot field goal to extend the lead with 27 seconds left. We're just about finished here.

    Recent findings suggest that LA has the ball at the Packers 6-yard line on 2nd-and-1. One more first down should end the game.

    Blake Corum is up to 155 yards on 31 rushes today as the Rams are close to putting this one away with a few big first downs. Packers are out of timeouts and we're under 3 minutes to play.

    Sources indicate that emmanuel Forbes leaps to intercept Jordan Love on another deep ball. Rams take over at their own 27 with 3:39 to go. Love's second INT of the day is a costly one for the Packers, who are running out of time.

    Industry observers note that the substantial Blake Corum run helps deliver some critical points for LA on a 40-yard Brandon McManus field goal. That makes it a two-possession game with 6:13 to play.

    Corum ripped off a 35-yard gain on 3rd-and-1 to set up the Rams in scoring position.

    Sources indicate that another empty offensive possession for Green Bay, which swiftly punts the ball away. Rams take over with 11:01 to play.

    The Rams drove all the way to the Packers 40-yard line but Stafford's pass is incomplete on 3rd-and-6. Green Bay gets the ball back at their own 11 with 12 minutes to play.

    Two plays after the Matthew Stafford interception, Jordan Love threw one.

    There appeared to be some miscommunication between Love and wide receiver Matthew Golden.

    Rams safety Jaylen McCollough capitalized, collecting the takeaway.

    That's a missed opportunity for the Packers in L.A. territory.

    Matthew Stafford just threw his 11th interception of the season.

    Packers linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper was sitting in the passing lane and interrupted the over route Rams tight end Tyler Higbee was running.

    Recent findings suggest that hopper returned the pick 21 yards to the L.A. 43-yard line.

    Instead of answering L.A.'s touchdown drive, Green Bay went three-and-out.

    It has been revealed that it almost was worse for the Packers. Jordan Love was nearly picked off by Rams safety Quentin Lake, who jumped a pass intended for wideout Savion Williams.

    On his ninth rushing attempt of the drive, Rams running back Blake Corum plunged into the end zone from a yard out.

    It has been revealed that him plowing into the paint put L.A. ahead 20-13 with 6:58 left in the third quarter.

    On third-and-goal, Rams wide receiver Konata Mumpfield came back to a ball Matthew Stafford threw to the pylon.

    Recent findings suggest that mumpfield appeared to make the touchdown grab. That's what was called, after all. Upon review, however, it was ruled that the receiver didn't complete the process of the catch.

    But there was a defensive holding penalty on the play, meaning that the Rams got a fresh set of downs at the goal line as a result of the play.

    Facing a third-and-8, Matthew Stafford moved the chains with a 20-yard pass to wide receiver Konata Mumpfield, who's up to 69 receiving yards on four grabs.

    Rams tight end Davis Allen is also out for the remainder of the game with an ankle injury that he reportedly suffered on L.A.'s first-half touchdown drive.

    Christian Watson was able to come back from a thigh injury in the first quarter, but he won't be returning in the second half now that he's dealing with a concussion.

    That's a tough blow for the Packers, who will be without their top wideout over the final two quarters of play.

    A roller-coaster first half at SoFi Stadium ended with the score tied 13-13.

    Recent findings suggest that the Rams scored on their first three possessions and staked themselves to a 13-3 advantage. Since, the Packers have stormed back.

    It has been revealed that green Bay wideout Christian Watson has caught four passes for 65 yards and a touchdown, but he's dealt with two injury problems. He's now being evaluated for a concussion.

    Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons recorded a long-awaited sack near the end of the first half.

    Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford has thrown for 98 yards on 12-of-15 passing.

    Micah Parsons just declared his return to NFL action with a sack of Matthew Stafford.

    With halftime nearing, Parsons dropped Stafford for a loss of 8 yards on first-and-10.

    Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (771 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.
    • But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.
    • Sources indicate that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.

    But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.

    Sources indicate that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off. That exceeded about $3 billion in notional volume for Kalshi's prediction markets on the same day.

    Sources indicate that perps are futures-style contracts where there is no expiration and traders do not need to own the underlying asset. Contracts instead continuously track the price of an asset, with funding payments to keep the contract price aligned with that of the market. Funding payments are made periodically between holders of short or long positions.

    Perps trading surpassed event contracts one day in September, but on Friday perps topped prediction markets volume for a second day. Now Kalshi expects that performance to continue as it introduces perps tied to more individual stocks. On Monday, for example, Kalshi introduced contracts linked to Anthropic.

    Recent findings suggest that kalshi was the first to debut perps in the U.S. after winning federal regulatory approval in May to list perps tied to cryptocurrencies.

    Perps trading volume includes any leverage that speculators acquire along with their trade, while event contracts are fully collateralized — for now.

    Since the original launch in May, Kalshi has received approval to introduce perps tied to metals, crude oil, stock indexes and individual stocks.

    According to recent reports, offshore perps — those available on exchanges not regulated in the U.S. — generated more than $90 trillion in notional trading volume in 2025, so it's not surprising that the product has grown so rapidly on Kalshi, according to Udesh Jha, chief risk officer at Kalshi Klear, the manufacturer's clearing house.

    It has been revealed that "We're just in very early innings. We're launching products, we're growing the participant base.".

    According to recent reports, perps were Kalshi's first product to mark its transition from a prediction market-focused platform to a full-blown financial exchange where various assets are traded. Last week, reports said that Kalshi is planning to offer trading on equities on its platform in the coming months.

    Sources indicate that at the same time, the company's perps product has come under fire. Some incumbent exchanges where futures are traded — which saw their stock prices decline following the approval of U.S. perps — believe the product was improperly approved. CME Group is suing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal derivatives regulator, for approving perps.

    Industry observers note that others have simply expressed concerns about the efficiency of the markets. CNBC previously reported that trading volume on Kalshi's most popular perps markets — tied to bitcoin and ether cryptocurrencies — was dramatically greater than open interest, or cash actively in the markets. It's a phenomenon that isn't common with U.S.-regulated traditional futures, nor other offshore perps markets.

    Kalshi said at the time it has "zero concerns" about the distinction, and that it appears because less leverage is offered compared to offshore exchanges and there are fewer incentives for traders to park capital on its perps markets.

    While Kalshi started with cryptocurrencies, Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street, noted perps tied to individual stocks likely represent the most promising opportunity for growth in the U.S.

    In a recent development, "That's how I foresee the way perps will penetrate further into traditional asset classes," Lau mentioned. "Perps on single stocks and [key performance indicators on individual companies] could change how investors hedge their portfolio or even make a directional bet.".

    In a recent development, kalshi's growth has been powered by the fact that right now it's the only exchange that can actively list perps in the U.S., though crypto exchange Coinbase received approval in May to route U.S. consumers to offshore platforms for trading. That monopoly status, however, will probably prove short lived.

    Coinbase has filed to list single-stock perps in the U.S., and President Donald Trump in August noted the CFTC is working to bring Hyperliquid — a dominant player in offshore perps activity — to domestic traders.

    But Jha at Kalshi isn't worried about the competition.

    "What will carry us is ... making sure that we have the right products for the marketplace, making sure we have the right surveillance of the products that we are trading.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
    • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
    • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

    Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

    The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

    “England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his upcoming club.

    Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

    Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

    Leeds manager Daniel Farke mentioned: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

    “I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

    “He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

    Sources indicate that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

    Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

    Industry observers note that forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

    Industry observers note that glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

    “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

    “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

    This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

    Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

    According to recent reports, the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

    It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

    Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

    “Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

    Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

    Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

    Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

    You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

    Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

    Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

    The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

    Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

    Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon mentioned: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

    Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

    "There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

    "It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

    A tough night for the home teams...

    And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

    Industry observers note that A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

    A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

    There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

    Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

    There will be six minutes of added time.

    That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

    Recent findings suggest that calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

    Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

    There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

    The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

    Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu introduces a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

    It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

    Industry observers note that jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

    The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

    Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

    According to recent reports, stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

    Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

    He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

    There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s newly introduced-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

    The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

    Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

    Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

    Industry observers note that chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

    Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

    According to recent reports, end-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE.

    Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

    This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

    Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

    According to recent reports, dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

    Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

    James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

    Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

    A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

    Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

    This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

    Industry observers note that both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

    James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

    Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

    It has been revealed that should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

    Leeds have only won four from 10.

    According to recent reports, what a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

    James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

    Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

    In a recent development, and, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

    Sources indicate that another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

    Recent findings suggest that ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

    Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

    In a recent development, elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

    Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

    Sources indicate that another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

    According to recent reports, what a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

    Sources indicate that nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

    It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

    Recent findings suggest that tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

    Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

    According to recent reports, the game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

    Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

    In a recent development, A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w.

    Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

    Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

    Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

    Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

    Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

    Recent findings suggest that dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

    Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

    Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

    James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

    Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

    Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

    Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

    Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

    Recent findings suggest that the first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”.

    Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9.

    Sources indicate that reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

    “I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

    “We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

    Industry observers note that previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”.

    When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a significant believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”.

    The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

    🏆x4⃣ pic.twitter.com/DRPXFa2kM3.

    This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

    Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

    Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

    Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

    Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

    Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood.

    Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi.

    Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha.

    Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin.

    The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

    Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

    It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

    Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

    📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi.

    Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

    Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj.

    Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s newly introduced head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

    Sources indicate that the Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

    Recent findings suggest that daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

    Tech Report: AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (974 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.
    • Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.
    • Sources indicate that huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

    Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

    Sources indicate that huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

    In a recent development, coreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, the spread on the neocloud organization's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

    Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

    Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect.".

    The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he said.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

    It has been revealed that coreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

    Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

    "A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he stated. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty.".

    It has been revealed that while Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

    With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

    During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress mentioned during the company's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

    That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

    "That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he mentioned.

    Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

    "[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

    After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "big trouble.".

    "Now that he's back, they're not," he said.

    Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

    "Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy said in a note Monday.

    Nvidia noted on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

    Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

    "These issues have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," noted economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

    John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

    Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

    "The tech giant is doing everything in its power to execute," he stated. "They don't need the high yield market at this time.".

    In a recent development, in the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a probe. At the federal level, President Trump mentioned Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    "There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg said. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file.".

    Industry News: NFL Thanksgiving Day preview: Eagles QB Joe Milton hopes to spoil Cowboys' hopes in his old home

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The middle game of the Thanksgiving trio — the stuffing, if you will — lacks the meat and potatoes of the first and final games of the day.
    • In a recent development, the 5-6 Cowboys host the 3-7 Eagles in a game that matters to Dallas.
    • They're only 3-2 in that stretch, and the NFC East-leading Giants have kept that same pace.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The middle game of the Thanksgiving trio — the stuffing, if you will — lacks the meat and potatoes of the first and final games of the day. But Eagles at Cowboys still carries some potential playoff importance.

    In a recent development, the 5-6 Cowboys host the 3-7 Eagles in a game that matters to Dallas. The Cowboys' offense has hit its stride recently, scoring 40 and 51 points, respectively, the past two games. Over the past five games, Dallas hasn't scored fewer than 27.

    The problem? They're only 3-2 in that stretch, and the NFC East-leading Giants have kept that same pace.

    The other problem? Dallas' defense. There were modest signs of improvement on that side of the ball in Mike Pettine's first game calling plays, especially compared to how the defense played against the 49ers. And for the first game possibly all season, the Cowboys could make a strong claim that they had the better defense — the Titans are that bad now, yes.

    In a recent development, the Eagles limped into the bye with seven straight losses, but they're coming off one of their best efforts of the season in beating the Steelers on Sunday. Defensively, they kept the Steelers under wraps for most of the four quarters and gave QB Joe Milton and the offense a chance.

    Sources indicate that milton returns to Dallas, where he spent parts of the past two seasons and saw action in four games last season behind Dak Prescott. Now Milton gets a chance to take on his former QB1 on Thursday after signing with the Eagles after Jalen Hurts landed on injured reserve.

    It has been revealed that the Cowboys left Milton, a preseason star the past two years, unprotected on their practice squad, and the Eagles gladly scooped him up. He has a chance to make the Cowboys pay for letting him walk — and before one of the biggest TV audiences Milton might have.

    The Eagles' playoff hopes hover at less than 1%, according to Next Gen Stats. The Cowboys, however, are still alive at 22%, barely above the Commanders (21%) and behind the Giants (65%).

    A loss would be pretty devastating. But beating Philadelphia would give the Cowboys a 3-1 mark in the division, which is the one edge they have right now on the Giants, who are 2-1-1 in NFC East games. The East could come down to the Week 17 Giants-Cowboys game, but every divisional matchup counts.

    Industry observers note that the Eagles, however, didn't look like a team ready to mail it in on Sunday. They showed some renewed vitality after the bye, with the team giving some younger players opportunities to stand out, including Milton. For Milton, there's personal pride on the line after spending parts of the past two years in Dallas, facing a defense that has plenty to prove.

    When the Eagles traded Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, it shone the spotlight more on Jalen Carter, who started this season slowly but whose play has been on the rise lately. In Sunday's upset of the Steelers, Carter was active and effective despite suffering a quad injury just prior to the game. He was a full participant in practice this week, but the player he might have faced off against, Cowboys right guard Tyler Booker, did not practice and is not expected to play Thursday. The Eagles know they have to slow down Dallas' passing attack and pressure Dak Prescott, and the best way to do that might be to detonate the operation from the inside. Carter and the Eagles also can't have a repeat of the last meeting, in Week 7, when Dallas ran for 204 yards on 38 carries.

    Sources indicate that sportsbooks opened this game Cowboys -1.5 in the summer — now it's -8.5. Losing Jalen Hurts for the season, along with a 3-7 record (and a putrid 2-8 record against the spread) will do that. Philadelphia put up a spirited defensive effort in a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers as 3.5-point home underdogs on Sunday, but this Dallas offense will provide a much stiffer test. Eagles starting QB Joe Milton and Philadelphia collected only 11 first downs and 214 yards of total offense; that's not going to get it done. Dak Prescott & Co. can't control how well a rejuvenated defense plays under Mike Pettine, but the Cowboys have scored at least 27 points in each of the past five games. Dallas scored 51 points against Tennessee on Sunday; the Eagles have scored 40 points combined in their past three contests. The Eagles D will put up a good fight, but barring several turnovers, I don't believe it will be able to keep up with Dallas. Cowboys -2.5 is another good teaser leg to go with that Packers +8.5, which cashed on Wednesday. — Ben Fawkes.

    Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub.

    In a recent development, we always expect plentiful points in any Dallas game, even with a struggling Philadelphia offense on the other side. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the middle of the three Thanksgiving games.

    1. What version of Saquon Barkley do we see? Barkley is expected to play despite a neck injury, but he hasn't been a high-volume back in 2026. Last week's 17 touches against the Steelers were actually his high for the year, which tells you a lot about Philly's season. This is also the worst Philadelphia offensive line in several years.

    2. How involved will George Pickens be? Dallas seemed to lose the plot with Pickens a few weeks ago, sending him just 10 targets over a two-week period (including a 4-57-1 game against Philadelphia). Since then, Dak Prescott has peppered both Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, and the Cowboys have scored 91 points over two weeks. Several teams in the NFL employ wide usage trees. Dallas doesn't want to be one of them.

    3. Is DeVonta Smith ready to pop? Smith saw plenty of opportunity in the win over Pittsburgh (12 targets), though he returned a modest 5-41-0 line. The Eagles have a capped ceiling with Joe Milton at quarterback, but at least they're trying to get Smith going. Dallas' secondary has been torched for most of the season. — Scott Pianowski.

    Tech Report: Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the company's board to rehire Huang.
    • Recent findings suggest that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," stated Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-organization director.
    • Industry observers note that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the company's board to rehire Huang. But investigations into the company, its executive leadership and its board continue as outside criticism mounts.

    Recent findings suggest that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," stated Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-organization director. "The board failed," she said, when it initially allowed Huang's removal. "The board's role is to think of all stakeholders.".

    Industry observers note that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors. "There is classic corporate securities law on the books in California that prevents investors and the public from being misled by companies," Bonta mentioned on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday.

    Directors are already defendants in a shareholder lawsuit accusing them of failing to oversee Nvidia. A separate securities class action targets the firm and Huang, its co-founder.

    Now the board’s insurance choices are part of the story. A risk advisor with direct knowledge of Nvidia’s coverage notes the company built an approximately $1 billion D&O tower, insurance jargon for directors and officers insurance policies from different companies that combine to cover one massive risk.

    According to recent reports, nvidia "loves insurance," the advisor said. “They buy insurance as if they have no balance sheet.” A billion-dollar tower would essentially mean Nvidia "bought the market," purchasing all the coverage it could get, according to an industry expert with 25 years working in financial insurance. The expert asked not to be named out of concern for past or potential future clients.

    In a recent development, but Nvidia directed all that coverage to Side A only, according to CNBC's source. Side A protects directors and officers personally when the company cannot indemnify them. Side B covers the company for legal defense costs or settlements on behalf of directors and officers, and Side C protects the company when it's named as a defendant in a suit such as a securities claim.

    The risk advisor says Nvidia believed it had "the war chest" to protect itself against a securities class action suit.

    Industry observers note that that choice is raising questions about whether the board protected itself at the firm’s expense. CNBC asked Nvidia for comment but received no response.

    An insurance CEO characterized a billion-dollar policy as a lot of coverage, but remarked a Side A-only allocation was a surprising move because it results in imbalanced coverage, protecting only directors.

    Recent findings suggest that that structure is not automatically a governance failure, according to a D&O insurance expert with long experience in coverage for banks, drugmakers and other businesses that often face litigation. Side A-only programs are common among companies with the capital to manage the corporate risk internally.

    Industry observers note that "For a tech giant with Nvidia’s resources, retaining the company-side risk can make financial sense," the advisor noted. It's Side A D&O that's "imperative to corporate governance.".

    Recent findings suggest that "It is a capital-allocation decision," the expert told me. The manufacturer decides that buying insurance for its own balance sheet is not worth the premium. In other words, Side B and Side C are considered too expensive for the coverage the company gets.

    The question for shareholders is whether the board’s decision to hold that risk was a sound use of the company’s resources and whether the company can absorb the costs if the claims grow.

    A shareholder derivative complaint filed Nov. 11 names Huang, directors and other officers. It alleges that they failed to oversee risks involving Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and made misleading statements. It also alleges that some defendants sold roughly $2 billion in Nvidia stock while holding material nonpublic information. Those remain allegations, not findings.

    A separate securities class action, filed Nov. 9, names Nvidia and Huang. It seeks damages for investors who bought Nvidia shares between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, alleging the organization and Huang misled investors.

    The distinction matters: The derivative suit is brought on Nvidia’s behalf, while the class action seeks recovery for investors.

    According to recent reports, "Insurance is already at work," states Michel Léonard, chief economist at the Insurance Information Institute, describing standard policy mechanics, not Nvidia’s specific policy. "Once the suit is filed, D&O starts paying defense costs, long before anyone proves anything.".

    According to recent reports, A claim still has to meet the policy’s terms, and defense costs can reduce the remaining limits. Nor does a drop in Nvidia’s market value by itself establish an insurable loss. Plaintiffs would need to prove legally recoverable damages; the policy would respond only to covered losses.

    In a recent development, the board has already taken steps it indicates are aimed at accountability. Nvidia declared an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and independent directors retained outside counsel two days later. Huang resigned as CEO and a director on Nov. 11; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Nvidia mentioned it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised by Huang's extramarital relationships.

    Recent findings suggest that atkins, who joined the board of Wynn Resorts in 2018 after founder Steve Wynn resigned, argues that allegations are not conclusions and that boards should also weigh governance concerns against the value a founder brings to a firm’s innovation. Nvidia's investigation is continuing even as Huang resumes leadership.

    “Will companies’ hyper-accelerated innovation speed be the same without them? I don’t think so,” noted Atkins, author of "Don't Waste a Board Seat: A Decision-Maker's Guide to Choosing Directors Who Create Value.".

    Industry observers note that nvidia’s 2026 proxy also indicates the company has indemnity agreements with its directors and officers — separate from its insurance. Those agreements provide for the company to cover certain costs and liabilities when the law permits.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Early in the second quarter Wednesday night in NBA Cup group play, LeBron James pulled up from Broad Street.
    • He drilled a 35-foot 3-pointer amid a torrid stretch that saw him make a trio of triples and score 14 straight points for the 76ers on Thanksgiving Eve.
    • While becoming the oldest player in NBA history to notch a triple double — at 41 years and 330 days old — James continued his recent hot streak from beyond the arc, going 4 of 6 on 3-point attempts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Early in the second quarter Wednesday night in NBA Cup group play, LeBron James pulled up from Broad Street.

    He drilled a 35-foot 3-pointer amid a torrid stretch that saw him make a trio of triples and score 14 straight points for the 76ers on Thanksgiving Eve. Before that sequence, the Sixers were trailing the Miami Heat by three points at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena. Afterward, they were up eight.

    While becoming the oldest player in NBA history to notch a triple double — at 41 years and 330 days old — James continued his recent hot streak from beyond the arc, going 4 of 6 on 3-point attempts. Philadelphia shot 14 of 35 from long range en route to a 111-104 victory.

    The Heat (10-7) would have clinched East Group B had they come out on top, but Philadelphia (15-4) denied Miami an eighth consecutive win, despite losing Jaylen Brown to a hamstring injury late in the first half and Joel Embiid being sidelined by illness.

    Nick Nurse's squad is now 2-1 in NBA Cup competition; Erik Spoelstra's Heat dropped to that same mark.

    Recent findings suggest that james finished with a season-high 25 points and 12 assists, plus 10 rebounds, with maybe his most notable dime taking place in the infancy of the fourth quarter. The 22-time All-Star flexed his elite court vision, timing a halfcourt lob perfectly to connect with VJ Edgecombe for a layup. James later dialed up an alley-oop for forward Dominick Barlow to throw down.

    Edgecombe was among the Sixers players stepping up in the absence of Brown and Embiid, as Philadelphia protected its nine-point halftime lead and kept Miami at arm's length over the final two quarters. He had 18 points, and Tyrese Maxey poured in 30.

    The Heat, who wound up trailing by 16 late in the final frame, were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, who clocked out with 32 points, 14 rebounds and 4 assists.

    Kevin Durant is now one of five NBA players to score 33,000 points. The 38-year-old Houston Rockets forward achieved that feat on Wednesday night in a 116-104 home victory against the Phoenix Suns. He joined James, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant.

    Durant did so while piling up 20 points for Houston (14-5), which, despite already being eliminated from NBA Cup knockout-round contention, kept pace in the upper echelon of the Western Conference standings.

    The Rockets improved to 2-2 in Cup group play, while the Suns (9-8) slid to 1-2. They, too, have been eliminated from knockout-round contention in West Group A.

    According to recent reports, along the way, Houston center Alperen Şengün passed Hakeem Olajuwon for the second-most triple-doubles in franchise history. Şengün, only 24 years old, secured his 15th performance of that kind with 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists.

    Late in the game, Suns wing Dillon Brooks got into it with Durant and was ejected after receiving his second technical foul of the night.

    Although the Minnesota Timberwolves lost LaMelo Ball to an ankle injury Wednesday, they held on to defeat the Oklahoma City Thunder 113-106.

    According to recent reports, jaden McDaniels came through, big time, in the West Group B matchup. In fact, by game's end, he was the third player in Wolves history to log at least 30 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists in consecutive games. That elite organization also includes Karl-Anthony Towns and Kevin Garnett.

    After going for 34 points, 10 rebounds and 6 assists on Monday in a win over the Brooklyn Nets, McDaniels put up 32 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists this time out versus the Thunder (10-9), who are 2-7 in their last nine games and eliminated from Cup knockout-round contention.

    Recent findings suggest that minnesota (14-5), on the other hand, is atop West Group B with a 3-0 record. McDaniels beat the third-quarter buzzer with a ridiculous off-balance shot. A late 3-pointer from Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu helped seal the deal.

    Note: "E —" denotes teams that have been eliminated from knockout round contention, whereas "Y —" denotes teams that have clinched their NBA Cup division.

    Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest substantial-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.
    • Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.
    • But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest substantial-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

    Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

    But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

    Recent findings suggest that “A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

    “We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

    "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

    Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

    The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

    A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

    Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

    Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

    Recent findings suggest that what a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

    “We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi stated. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

    Sources indicate that cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

    Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

    Industry observers note that buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

    Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

    Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

    The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

    Recent findings suggest that “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against massive teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.
